problem_checks.analysis: The two-point compact system satisfies the stated ASP/MCGBP hypotheses and gives exactly 26/25 > 22/25 and, in the small-radius case, 199/250000 > 51/125000. These refute the specified sufficient estimates; the smaller example still satisfies the final radius conclusion. Neither is a counterexample to Proposition3.2. The radius derivation controls Lemma3.8 and Proposition3.2, which p7 explicitly uses for Theorem2.1(I). The replacement reserves half the distance cost, takes the corrected constants independently of the periodic orbit, and proves nonnegative block averages plus strictly positive reserved cost off the orbit. It preserves the original coefficient and all permitted perturbations. Repairability does not remove a false core proof step.

The source norm is sup plus Lipschitz seminorm. On the length-two circle with a singleton orbit, the distance perturbation has norm 2 epsilon, and uniform approximation forces 4 epsilon - 3 eta > 2 epsilon + eta in the stated regime. A high-frequency sine meets arbitrarily small uniform radius and the derivative-only bound while lying outside the substituted full-norm ball, so the proof changes the every-perturbation quantifier. Proposition3.9 and3.1 are explicitly used on p18 for Theorem2.1(II). The checked replacement extracts only the seminorm estimate epsilon+2 eta, controls different components using their positive minimum separation, and obtains full norm below8.75 epsilon within the original10 epsilon budget for every allowed perturbation. This is a core derivation defect, not a counterexample to the repaired C1 conclusion or an assertion of false Lipschitz density.

The four local formulas omit w, change the escape threshold, reverse a required inequality, and count a remainder incorrectly.
